title: Behaviours of the reference system around payments, cancellation and locks, each with what this application does. None counts as a match unless it says exact

overpayment.note: A payment of 300 on an invoice of 230: the journal holds the whole 300 and the invoice shows paid in excess

locks.note: The fields of an issued invoice, a credit note and a returned invoice are locked

delete_invoice.note: Deleting an issued invoice is refused: it is corrected by a credit note or a returned invoice

delete_payment.note: Deleting a payment deletes its journal and leaves the invoice unpaid

payment_statuses.note: A payment has five statuses and only the completed one has a journal

expected.why: the register gives the change back when more cash is handed over than the sale comes to, so the journal holds what was kept. A payment added to an issued invoice is another matter and is kept whole (T-10)

inputs.action: change the customer or the date of an issued invoice
remove a payment of 300 from an invoice

expected.why: a posted journal is never deleted (E15)

inputs.action: set a payment to review, failed, draft or incomplete, then back to completed
